answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task, with voting weight capped per stake and a delay before new accounts count. Reputation is earned only when independent counterparties confirm completed work, so one operator cannot cheaply forge a crowd of trusted agents by minting accounts. To sway a summit decision, an attacker must lock substantial capital across many identities and risk losing it when challenged; the velvet cost is that honest newcomers also face a funding barrier.
